title: Socially Responsible Behaviors of Nursing Students in Private Universities in Santiago, Chile: A Study on the Alignment with Sustainable Development Goals.
content: This study investigates the socially responsible behaviors of nursing students at private universities in Santiago, Chile, focusing on their alignment with sustainable development values. Social responsibility, viewed as an ethical obligation toward society, is essential in preparing healthcare professionals to tackle global health and social challenges. The research utilized the Inventory of Socially Responsible Behaviors in University Students (ICOSORE-U) to assess nursing students’ engagement in social, academic, and civic responsibilities. A sample of 400 nursing students from four private universities participated, with an equal gender distribution. The data were analyzed through exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis (EFA and CFA) to assess the validity and reliability of the scale. The findings confirm that the ICOSORE-U scale effectively measures socially responsible behaviors, identifying key factors such as social assistance, respect, cultural citizenship, and academic responsibility. Notably, no significant demographic differences were found in students' social responsibility scores, indicating that nursing education programs universally foster these behaviors. This study underscores the importance of integrating social responsibility into nursing curricula to ensure that future nurses are not only clinically competent but also committed to ethical, sustainable practices in healthcare. These findings provide valuable insights into how nursing education can support the development of socially responsible behaviors, contributing to the enhancement of nursing programs and the promotion of sustainable healthcare practices aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
